title.mn: To be үйл үг: эерэг хэлбэр

promise.en: By the end, you can introduce yourself and describe anyone.
promise.mn: Энэ хичээлийн төгсгөлд өөрийгөө танилцуулж, бусдыг дүрсэлж чадна.

slides.say: The verb to be. It is the most common verb in English. By the end of this video you can introduce yourself and describe anyone you know.

explain.en: am, is, are: three forms of one verb.
explain.mn: am, is, are: нэг үйл үгийн гурван хэлбэр.

slides.say: Read the lines as Anu, warmly and simply. Five short sentences, and she has told us her name, her age, her town and her family. [click] Now look at the small words in blue: am, is, are. One of them is in every sentence. They are three forms of the same verb.
slides.teach: A Mongolian name and a Mongolian town make the English feel like something the student could say tomorrow. Use full forms here; short forms arrive on slide 7.

explain.mn: Аль үгс is-тэй хамт ордог вэ?

slides.say: Read each twice. Then name the pairs: I with am. She with is. They with are. It with is. Ask the question you will answer on the next slide: which words go with is?
slides.teach: The order deliberately mixes the three forms so the student has to search for the pattern rather than receive it.

callout.en: One verb, three forms. The subject decides.
callout.mn: Нэг үйл үг, гурван хэлбэр. Өгүүлэгдэхүүн шийднэ.

slides.say: Now we name it: the verb to be, to be үйл үг. In the present it has three forms, and the subject decides which one. [click] I always takes am. Only I. [click] He, she and it take is. [click] You, we and they take are.
slides.teach: Point out that am goes with exactly one word in the whole language. That fact alone makes it stick.

explain.en: Swap it for a pronoun in your head, then choose.
explain.mn: Толгойдоо төлөөний үгээр орлуулж бодоод, дараа нь сонго.

slides.say: Usually we don't say he or they. We use a name or a noun. So how do you choose? Swap it for a pronoun in your head. Bat is a he, so Bat is. My parents are they, so my parents are. One thing: is. More than one: are.
slides.teach: The swap trick is the most useful tool in the lesson because it works on any subject, however long. Say it as a habit: swap, then choose.

slides.say: To be connects a person to information about them. There are four kinds. [click] Who or what someone is: a name, a job, a nationality. [click] What someone is like: how they look, how they feel. [click] Where someone is, or where they come from. [click] And age. In English, age uses be: I am 14.
slides.teach: Age is the one that surprises. The correct forms are I am 14 or I am 14 years old. I am 14 years on its own is wrong, and I have 14 years is wrong. Say this as the closing line of the slide.

callout.en: The apostrophe ( ' ) shows a missing letter.
Short forms for speaking, full forms for formal writing.
callout.mn: Ярихдаа товч хэлбэр, албан бичигт бүтэн хэлбэр.

slides.say: In speaking, people almost always use the short forms. The apostrophe shows where a letter is missing: I am becomes I'm, and the a is gone. Both forms are correct. Short forms for speaking and friendly writing, full forms for formal writing. [click] Now listen to how they sound. Say each sentence slowly, then at natural speed. I'm a student sounds almost like one word.
slides.teach: Students sometimes think short forms are slang; make clear they are standard English. Two sound notes worth saying aloud: they're sounds exactly like there and their, and we're rhymes with here, not with her.

context.en: Mongolian needs no verb here. English always does.
context.mn: Монголоор: Би сурагч. Англиар: I am a student.

slides.say: In Mongolian, Би сурагч has no verb and needs none. English always needs one. So not She very happy, but She is very happy. [click] Same with age: My brother is 12 years old. [click] And the third: my parents are two people, so are.
slides.teach: The first two are the classic Mongolian-speaker mistake and appear in speech for years if not fixed early. The third catches students who pick the form by habit instead of by counting.

lines.en: My father **is** an engineer, and my mother **is** a nurse.
lines.mn: Аав маань инженер, ээж маань сувилагч.

slides.say: Read each line twice. Point out that every single sentence has a form of be, that the speaker mixes full and short forms naturally, and that all four uses from slide 6 appear: name, age, place, job, description.
slides.teach: This is the student's own self-introduction waiting to be written. Change the name, age, town and jobs and it is theirs.

cards.en: I **am** · he / she / it **is** · you / we / they **are**
Every English sentence needs a verb.
cards.mn: Англи өгүүлбэрт үйл үг заавал байна.

slides.say: Line one: the three forms. I am. He, she, it is. You, we, they are. [click] Line two: for any name or noun, swap it for a pronoun in your head, then choose. One thing, is. More than one, are. [click] Line three, the most important one for us. In Mongolian, Би сурагч has no verb. In English every sentence needs one: I am a student. Close: Now you can introduce yourself and describe anyone: their name, their job, what they are like, where they are from and how old they are. [click] Closing line (spoken, never on the slide): Одоо энэ видеоны доорх дасгалаар мэдлэгээ шалгаарай. Hold the slide silently for three seconds.
slides.teach: Say line three slowly and in both languages, because it is the habit that takes longest to break. Hold the slide silently for three seconds after the closing sentence.
